title: Service Call Cost Calculator: Callout Pricing
description: Build a service call's price from callout fee, mileage and labour with the Service Call Cost Calculator — quotes with the working shown. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, an $85 callout plus 36 miles at an example $0.67 a mile plus 1½ hours at $95 comes to $251.62 — every line of it explainable at the door.

faq: What does this tool calculate?
A service call's price: callout fee + (mileage rate × distance) + (hourly rate × hours), decomposed line by line.
Is it free to use?
Yes — for quoting your work or sanity-checking a bill you received.
How accurate is the result?
Exact for the rates and figures entered. Commercial accuracy — rates that truly cover your costs — starts with your cost-per-mile figure.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Travelling time is priced through your rates; traffic argues for a time-based mileage component, which is a tariff design choice.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Charge the road miles — the van travels those, and the customer's own map will agree with them.
Should the return journey be charged?
Most callout tariffs fold the return into the rate or the fee. State the convention on the quote and apply it to every job alike.
Do parts belong in the total?
Listed separately, usually — this calculator prices attendance and labour. A quote that hides parts inside a labour line invites the argument it deserves.
After-hours premiums?
Apply them to the labour line (or all lines) as your tariff states — the structure holds, the rates change costume.
Two technicians attend?
Labour doubles or the rate does; price the crew you send. The formula's shape is unchanged.
The customer supplies their own parts.
Then the parts line is zero and the quote says so — attendance and labour still price exactly as here.
